issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() should return an int (the task even hints to check the UML for the expected return type), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return a StudentCount object and adds a StudentCount class. This introduces a new return type not present in the problem or template and will confuse students: they will implement the method to return an int as instructed by the UML, but the solution (and any reference tests based on it) uses StudentCount, creating a structural mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the return type across all artifacts. Either (A) change the problem statement/UML and template to specify that getTotalNumberOfStudents() returns a StudentCount and include a StudentCount class in the template so students implement against that type, or (B) modify the solution to have getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (the sum of inscribed and guest students) and remove the StudentCount helper class, updating dependent methods (getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents, getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to use an int. Choose the option that preserves the intended learning objective and make the change consistently in problem, template, and solution.

issues.description: The concept 'total number of students' is specified in the problem statement and UML as an int return value for getTotalNumberOfStudents(), but the solution exposes that concept via a StudentCount class and returns StudentCount from getTotalNumberOfStudents(). This introduces a new identifier (StudentCount) for the same conceptual entity and a different public API type than the UML/template expect, creating a mapping barrier for students who are guided to implement/expect an int.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the public API with the problem/UML by making getTotalNumberOfStudents() return an int (e.g. public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents; }). If a StudentCount wrapper is desired internally, keep it private or provide an additional method, but do not change the method signature expected by the exercise/UML.
